 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 26-09-2023 at about 6.45 p.m. the petitioner was standing on the extreme left side of the road near Kasturinagar sky walk, Kasturi nagar service road to cross the road, at that time rider of two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-03/KR-3562 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Hosmat hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc.,
4.

It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 62 years and was doing Helper work in Private office and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03/KR-3562.
Hence, the jurisdictional K.R.Puram Traffic police have registered a criminal case against rider of said vehicle in Cr.No.332/2023.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.

6. After service of summons, respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal,
hence she was placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel &
filed the written statement.

7. The respondent No.2 filed the written statement and admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03/KR-3562 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contended that, the rider of offending vehicle does not posses valid D.L. on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 26.9.2023 at about 6-45 p.m., near Kasturi nagar Sky walk, Kasturi nagar service road, Bengalurudue to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registrationNo.KA-  03/KR-3562 in an actionable  negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3. What order or award?
9.
In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Shekhar M. as PW2 and got marked Ex.P12 to Ex.P14.

Further petitioner also got examined Medical Record Officer of Hosmat Hospital as PW3 and got marked documents Ex.P15 to Ex.P20.
10.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and got marked Ex.R1.
11.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

12. At the time of argument the counsel for petitioner has relied decision reported in Civil Appeal SLP (C) No.0351/2019) of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of Ranjeet and another V/s Abdul Kayam Neb and another.

entities.text: Ranjeet and another V/s Abdul Kayam Neb and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that "once a charge sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.
Even if the eye witness are not examined, that will not be fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to the negligence of the bus driver."

13. The counsel for respondent No.2 has relied upon decision reported in 2023 Live Law (SC) 531 - 2023 INSC 621 of our Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Mathew Alexander V/s Mohammed Shafi and another.

entities.text: Mathew Alexander V/s Mohammed Shafi and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, "the final report in criminal investigation connected to the accident would not have a bearing on the claim petition and that the claim petition must be considered on its own merits."

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:-
15.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03/KR-3562 the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

16. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
17. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
18. The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon police documents at Ex.
P1 to Ex
. P7. Ex.
P1-true copy of the F.I.R., Ex.P2-true copy of first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P4-true copy of the spot mahazar.

Ex. P5- true copy of the spot sketch,
Ex.P6-true copy of IMV report, and Ex-P7 is true copy of charge sheet.

19. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Ramakrishna M., the S.H.O. of K.R.Pura Police have registered the case in Cr.No.332/2023 against the rider of the offending two wheeler for the offences punishable under sections 279 & 337 of IPC R/W Section 134(1 & b) R/W Section 187 of IMV Act.

After completion of investigation, I.O. has filed the charge sheet against the rider of two wheeler for the above offences punishable under sections 279 & 337 of IPC R/W Section 134(1 & b) R/W Section 187 of IMV Act.
20.
On the other hand, to prove the defenses of the respondent No.2, relied on the evidence of RW1.
He has deposed in his evidence that, the alleged accident took place in the middle of the road and the pedestrian are not suppose to stand in the middle of the road.
Further as per the charge sheet there is a Sky walk meant for pedestrian, hence, there is gross violation of the traffic rules.
To prove the defence of the respondent No.2 he has not made an effort to examine the rider of the motor cycle or any independent eye witness.

Hence it is crystal clear that, in connection with the above issue,
evidence given by the petitioner is prevailing over the evidence of the respondent.

As such, the decision relied by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 is not applicable to the present case Rama Krishnan M vs Santhana Celina Savarimuthu on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104231824/
4 on hand.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the decision relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner
is aptly applicable to the facts of this case.

21. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1 though several questions put to this witness, nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the assertion of the petitioner against the rider of the offending vehicle and to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent.

22. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03-KR-3562.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
23.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

24. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P3.

The said document Rama Krishnan M vs Santhana Celina Savarimuthu on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104231824/
5 discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Left leg distal 1/3rd both bones fracture 26.

sentences.text: In connection with the above said injury the doctor is of the opinion that, the said injury is grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary issued by Hosmat Hospital as per Ex.P10 reveals that petitioner was admitted from 26.9.2023 to 28.9.2023.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Shekar as PW2.

He has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained cut lacerated wound 5x2 cms at distal 1/3rd of left leg, swelling,
tenderness and deformity of left leg, type open fracture both bones of left leg distal 1/3rd.
He has placed outpatient record, disability certificate and x-ray at Ex.P12 to Ex.P14.
Further examined Medical Record Officer as PW3.

She has placed authorisation letter, MLC extract, police intimation,
inpatient record, outpatient record and x-rays as per Ex.P15 to Ex.P20.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
27.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a helper at private office, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, there is no iota of documents to show that, he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In the absence of the documents, it is apt to be considered notional income of the petitioner.
On going through the discharge summary issued by Hosmat Hospital as per Ex.P10 reveals that petitioner was admitted from 26.9.2023 to 28.9.2023.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.

Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.32,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
28.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P11 to the extent of Rs.1,87,114/- along with advance receipts and prescriptions.
Except the suggestion, there are no contra materials available available on record to prove that the said medical bills are created and fabricated for the purpose of this case.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,87,114/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
29.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/-
towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
30.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P3 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Shekar M. examined as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained cut lacerated wound 5x2 cms at distal 1/3rd of left leg, swelling, tenderness and deformity of left leg,
type open fracture both bones of left leg distal 1/3rd.
For which petitienr underwent left tibia external fixation application on 27.9.2023.
He was regular follow-up in OPD.
Later admitted at Maiya Hospital on 8.11.2023, where he underwent external fixator removal of left leg and discharged on 9.11.2023.

Again he was admitted to Manipal Hospital, Jayanagar and underwent open reduction and internal fixation with plate and screws left tibia with left side iliac crest bone graftingt on 27.12.2023.
31.

Further, PW2 has stated that, at the time of examination of the petitioner, he has multiple scars over left leg, healed surgical scar over left iliac crest, mild pain in left leg on standing and walking.
He had restricted movements in left knee and ankle.

X-ray shows left leg malunited lower 1/3rd fracture both bones with tibia implant in situ and assessed disability of left lower limb at 48.91% and that of his whole body 16.30%.
32.
At the time of cross-examination of PW2, stated that he is not treated doctor and denied the suggestion that he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
33. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 as 16.30% disability of whole body.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 12%
instead of 16.30%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
34. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 62 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P8 for consideration.

On going through the said document,
the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 16.4.1960.
The accident occurred on 26.9.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 63 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '7' is to be taken into consideration.

35. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was working as a helper at private firm and getting an income of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not placed any documents to prove his income.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.

It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had Rama Krishnan M vs Santhana Celina Savarimuthu on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104231824/
7 taken place in the year 2023.

sentences.text: As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.

36. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.16,000 X 12 X 7 X 12/100= Rs.1,61,280/-.
Loss of amenities;
37.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he is completely bed ridden and cannot any work.
On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
38.
PW2 has stated that petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for achieving union, which would costs around Rs.25,000/-.
But, the petitioner has not placed any documents for consideration.
By taking into consideration of the evidence of PW2, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.

39. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 40,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 32,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.1,87,114-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 10,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.1,61,280-00 due to disability

6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.4,70,394-00 Rama Krishnan M vs Santhana Celina Savarimuthu on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104231824/

LIABILITY:
41.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-02-Z-5454 alleged accident had taken place.

The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1,
remained unshaken.
42. As per Ex.R1, the policy was valid from 8.5.2023 to 7.5.2028.
The alleged accident was taken place on 26.9.2023.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE N0.3:
43.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,70,394/- (Rupees four lakh seventy thousand three hundred and ninety four only), with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
